@MisteriumADP I partially disagree. I feel like you're oversimplifying things by saying no one is special and making problems out to be 'simple' or almost 'ridiculous.' No judgment here, but a lot of people deal with really heavy trauma. I'm not using that as an excuse to do nothing—we're ultimately in the driver's seat of our own lives—but we need to look at the whole story. Many people grow up completely alone and broken. They don't have a support system to teach them how to handle life's blows, much less deep trauma. Sure, self-help exists, but what about someone who has lost the will to live? Someone who has faced so much trauma they just can't take it anymore? Is telling them 'Your problems aren't special' actually going to help? What do they do next? 
 
We need to understand people's pain if we actually want to help them. A dose of tough love is necessary to move forward, but so is empathy. I like your perspective, but I think it only works when someone is already halfway out of the hole.
